title: Cross-variant quantized kernel selector caused first-token throughput loss; mitigation plan
creator: Liam Chen
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden regressions in first-token latency (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec drops across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after the 2.6.1 kernel-selector rollout that favours int8/uint8 paths. This ticket captures the investigation, temporary mitigations, and a deployment plan to restore baseline performance while we prepare a robust fix.
impact_summary: Beginning 2026-03-04 03:00 UTC, we observed 10-40% increase in p95 TTFT and 20-60% drop in tokens/sec for several long-context payloads on models using the quantized-serving variants. Affected customers: acme-ml (hosted), FinLine (dedicated VPC), and MedVault (private on-prem). Escalation SLAs triggered by FinLine and MedVault. No data exfiltration; functional correctness preserved but UX is degraded.
reproduction_steps: 1) Route 1k concurrent short-chat requests (avg prompt 320 tokens) to quant-int8 model variant on region us-west-2.
2) Observe increase in queueing on the model backends and new backpressure signals in the router.
3) Measure TTFT (first byte) using synthetic harness: p50 ~ 85ms -> baseline 40ms; p95 ~ 420ms -> baseline 280ms.
4) Compare kernel selection logs: majority switched to int8 GEMM kernels after selector rollout (selector v1.12) at 2026-03-03 22:00 UTC.
5) Reproduces across hosted/dedicated/private with same model family when using the int8-config profile and long-context priming (>=512).
investigation_notes: Telemetry correlates spike to selector-v1.12 which adjusted kernel ranking weights to prefer int8 kernels for certain attention/MLP shapes.
Profiling on a failing worker showed increased time spent in KV cache serialization + int8 dequantization path; this introduces a blocking fence in the existing runtime path for contexts >512 tokens.

Root cause hypothesis: when int8 kernels are selected for this model/shape, warmup of quantized weights plus an extra copy path serializes requests that used to benefit from asynchronous KV reuse, causing TTFT and tokens/sec regression.
Dedicated VPC nodes with pinned NICs show similar behavior; private on-prem observed the same pattern but with different absolute latencies (hardware variance).
No single customer prompt causes regression — it's emergent under realistic load and context lengths; explains staggered customer reports.
Related telemetry: increased kernel-fallback counts (10x), elevated worker GC pauses (small bump), and router-level hedging spikes where hedged requests still hit delayed int8 backends.
Cross-check with model-ops: no model changes were pushed at the same time as selector rollout; confirms runtime change is likely culprit.
decision_log: 2026-03-05 10:30 UTC: Rollback of selector-v1.12 approved as immediate mitigation for Hosted while we validate targeted fixes (lead: Priya).
2026-03-05 12:00 UTC: For Dedicated customers, implement per-customer kernel-preference override via config flag router.preference.kernel=fp16 as a short-term guard.
2026-03-06 02:00 UTC: Private deployments notified with a patch and step-by-step toggling instructions; ops-runbook published to Confluence.

2026-03-07 18:00 UTC: Decided not to force a full platform-wide rollback to avoid destabilizing model families that saw neutral/positive perf with int8 — choose targeted routing overrides + quickfix in runtime.
2026-03-09 09:00 UTC: Engineering decided to implement an async-priming path for int8 warmup to avoid serialization, tracked as follow-up (see action item #2).
action_items: A1: Roll back selector-v1.12 on Hosted control-plane and pin kernel-ranking to previous weights (done 2026-03-05 11:15 UTC). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8419
A2: Implement async int8 weight priming + non-blocking KV cache handoff (in progress, branch: feature/async-priming). Estimate: 8 points.
A3: Expose per-customer router override config; devops task to apply to FinLine and MedVault (applied 2026-03-05 13:30 UTC).
A4: Add canary test in CI that runs synthetic long-context RTT/TTFT regression suite for quantized kernels (backfill tests by 2026-03-12).
A5: Create a rollback-safe telemetry alert to detect TTFT delta >20% on p95 for critical customers (rules authored: /infra/alerts/ttft-delta.yaml).
A6: Post-incident PRD: Evaluate kernel-ranking heuristics and add hardware-aware weighting to prevent regressions on mixed deployments (owner: Research/Applied ML).

postmortem_notes: Tentative RCA: selector-v1.12 introduced kernel-ranking changes without hardware-aware heuristics for long-context priming; this caused a synchronous int8 priming path that serializes KV handoff and inflates TTFT under load.
Mitigation effectiveness: Hosted rollback restored ~80% of baseline p95 TTFT. Dedicated override and private toggles restored affected customer SLAs but required manual ops intervention.
Follow-ups: add pre-deploy canaries that exercise long-context priming profiles, add per-variant performance baselines in model catalog, and implement hardware-aware kernel weights.
